title: Brakes keep working while a session waits on your answer
why: Your gripe, Oct 26: a local UI/UX session waited on your question while its background agents kept working; the Mac ran out of storage and they crashed. Once you answered, the session saw the brake at once.
note: Finding, Oct 26 (claude-settings main 54be9f1): the machine-load brake (c14) read memory and disk only on a lane-start call, so lanes already running were never braked, whatever the main session was doing. Built: PR 642 ("brake a running lane at a full machine", draft, head 46a9060). Each background agent's own shell command and file write reads the load inside the guard hook that already runs; at full it is refused and told to stop and report. The main session is never braked, so it can free space. Red on main, green on the branch; Sonnet review round 1 clear, its three notes fixed. Not built: a watcher (the mandate forbids a timer or long-lived process) and a 'pause while a question waits' rule (the brake no longer depends on the wait). Deferred: shiv's word on the per-write read, which bends outcomes-mechanize-rules and c14's 'no per-call reading'; on the waiting page, recommended keep as built. Mac proof brief: briefs/c77-running-lane-brake-mac-proof.md. Port: no, the guard installs from claude-settings into every repo already. Placed ahead of c75 (triage, Oct 26).
ask:
# c77: prove the running-lane brake on the Mac

Goal: prove that a background agent's own Bash call reaches the guard with its `agent_id`, so the running-lane brake (PR 642, "brake a running lane at a full machine") can stop it.

Steps, on the Mac, after PR 642 is installed (`sh install.sh` from a checkout of its branch, or after it merges):
1. In any repo, start one Agent with `run_in_background: true` whose only job is to run `echo probe` in Bash.
2. Read the last lines of `~/.claude/guard.log` (or the payload trace, if one is on). Report whether the Bash call's payload carried an `agent_id`.
3. Do not fill the disk to test the refusal. The fixture suite proves the refusal; this brief proves only the live payload.

Report (5 lines max): the commit installed, whether the background Bash payload carried `agent_id`, and anything unexpected.
